S001@7611-7692.words: do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work
S001@7611-7692.reason: The judgement says nearly all studies in the source have low confidence in their findings, which bears on how far the evidence on whether these programmes work can be trusted.

S001@7900-8058.reason: The judgement describes the problem (children with disabilities falling behind because schools aren't adapted to them) rather than giving evidence on whether any programme improves their education or which kinds work best.

S001@8059-8153.reason: The judgement concerns equalising health outcomes, whereas the question asks only about educational outcomes, and the scope excludes health interventions judged on clinical outcomes alone.

S001@8154-8406.reason: The judgement recommends a twin-track approach combining disability-specific support with mainstream inclusion (teacher skills, classroom accessibility), which bears directly on which programme types work best.

S001@8407-8703.reason: The judgement says most reviewed interventions targeted individual children rather than system- or school-level mainstreaming, which limits what the evidence can show about which programme types work best.

S001@8704-8859.reason: The judgement says evaluation should focus on interventions that target the child's broader environment as well as the individual, which bears on which programme types are best supported by evidence.
